sentences.zh: 呂安國

translations.literal: Lu Anguo
translations.idiomatic: Lu Anguo

sentences.zh: 呂安國，廣陵廣陵人也。

translations.literal: Lu Anguo was a native of Guangling in Guangling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Anguo was a man of Guangling in Guangling commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋大明末，安國以將領見任，隱重有幹局，爲劉勉所稱。

translations.literal: Late in the Daming era of Song, Anguo was appointed as a military commander; grave and weighty with capacity for affairs, he was praised by Liu Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song's Daming era, Anguo was named to command troops; steady and capable, he won praise from Liu Mian.

sentences.zh: ，勉征殷琰於壽春，安國以建威將軍爲勉軍副。

translations.literal: , when Mian campaigned against Yin Yan at Shouchun, Anguo served as General Who Establishes Might and was deputy to Mian's command.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian marched against Yin Yan at Shouchun, Anguo served as General Who Establishes Might and as Mian's second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 衆軍擊破琰長史杜叔寶軍於橫塘，安國抄斷賊糧道，燒其運車，多所傷殺。

translations.literal: The armies defeated Chief Clerk Du Shubao's force of Yan at Hengtang; Anguo raided to cut the rebel grain route, burned their transport carts, and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: The host broke Du Shubao, Yin Yan's chief clerk, at Hengtang; Anguo struck behind the lines to sever grain traffic, burned the supply carts, and killed a great number.

sentences.zh: 琰衆奔退，勉遣安國追之，先至壽春。

translations.literal: Yan's troops fled; Mian sent Anguo in pursuit, and he reached Shouchun first.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's men ran; Mian sent Anguo after them, and he came to Shouchun ahead of the rest.

sentences.zh: 琰閉門自守，安國與輔國將軍垣閎屯據城南，於是衆軍繼至。

translations.literal: Yan shut the gates and held firm; Anguo with General Who Assists the State Yuan Hong encamped south of the city, and then the main armies arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yan barred the gates and stood on the defense; Anguo and Yuan Hong, General Who Assists the State, held the south of the city, and the armies followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 安國勳第一，封彭澤縣男，未拜，明年，改封鍾武縣，加邑爲四百戶。

translations.literal: Anguo's merit ranked first; he was enfeoffed Baron of Pengze, but before he received the investiture, the next year he was re-enfeoffed at Zhongwu with fief increased to four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo's merit stood first; he was made baron of Pengze but had not yet been invested when, the next year, he was re-enfeoffed at Zhongwu and his fief rose to four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 累至寧朔將軍、義陽太守。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed by stages to General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，又改封湘南縣男。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was again re-enfeoffed Baron of Xiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was re-enfeoffed as baron of Xiangnan.

sentences.zh: 虜陷汝南，司州失守，以安國爲督司州諸軍事、寧朔將軍、司州刺史。

translations.literal: The northerners took Runan; Si Province was lost; Anguo was made overseer of all Si Province military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: The northern enemy seized Runan and Si Province fell; Anguo was named to oversee all Si Province forces, as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 六年，義陽立州治，仍領義陽太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Yiyang was established as the provincial seat; he still held the administration of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the seat of Yiyang was made a province; he still led Yiyang as administrator.

sentences.zh: 稍遷右軍將軍，假輔師將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General of the Right Army, acting General Who Assists the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised step by step to general of the right army, with acting rank as General Who Assists the Army.

sentences.zh: ，爲晉熙王征虜司馬，輔師將軍如故。

translations.literal: , and was made campaign staff officer on the Prince of Jinxi's conquest staff, General Who Assists the Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made staff officer on the Prince of Jinxi's conquest staff, with General Who Assists the Army unchanged.

sentences.zh: 轉游擊將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Raiding Attack.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to General of Raiding Attack.

sentences.zh: 三年，出爲持節、都督青兖冀三州緣淮前鋒諸軍事、輔師將軍、兖州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as bearer of the staff, overseer of Qing, Yan, and Ji Provinces along the Huai front-guard military affairs, General Who Assists the Army, and inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went out bearing the staff as overseer of Qing, Yan, and Ji along the Huai frontier, General Who Assists the Army, and inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 明年，進號冠軍將軍，還爲游擊將軍，加散騎常侍、征虜將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was advanced to General Who Commands the Champions, returned as General of Raiding Attack, with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry and General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was raised to General Who Commands the Champions, then returned as General of Raiding Attack with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry and General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，太祖以安國爲湘州刺史，征虜將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, the Founder made Anguo inspector of Xiangzhou, General Who Conquers the Barbarians as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, the Founder named Anguo inspector of Xiang, with General Who Conquers the Barbarians unchanged.

sentences.zh: 先是王蘊罷州，南中郎將南陽王翽未之鎮，蘊寧朔長史庾佩玉權行州事，朝廷先遣南中郎將中兵參軍臨湘令韓幼宗領軍防州。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Yun had left the inspector post; the Prince of Nanyang Hui had not yet gone to his command; Yun's chief secretary of pacifying the north Yu Peiyu held state affairs on an interim basis; the court had first sent Han Youzong, central-troops staff officer on the southern commander staff and magistrate of Linxiang, to lead troops guarding the province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Yun had left the province; Prince of Nanyang Hui had not yet taken up his post; Yu Peiyu, Yun's chief secretary of pacifying the north, held the province in his stead; the court had already sent Han Youzong, central-troops staff officer on the southern commander staff and magistrate of Linxiang, to guard the province with troops.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之之難，二人各相疑阻，佩玉輙殺幼宗。

translations.literal: During Shen Youzhi's troubles the two men mistrusted each other; Peiyu at once killed Youzong.
translations.idiomatic: In Shen Youzhi's crisis the two men blocked each other; Peiyu killed Youzong outright.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍黃回至郢州，遣軍主任候伯行湘州事，又殺佩玉。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Huang Hui reached Yingzhou and sent army-master Ren Houbo to act as Xiangzhou affairs; he also killed Peiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, General Who Pacifies the West, came to Ying and sent army-master Ren Houbo to handle Xiang affairs; he killed Peiyu as well.

sentences.zh: 候伯與回同衞將軍袁粲謀石頭事，回令候伯水軍乘舸往赴，會衆軍已至，不得入。

translations.literal: Houbo and Hui together with General of the Guard Yuan Can plotted the Stone citadel affair; Hui ordered Houbo's naval force in light boats to go, but the armies had already arrived and they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Houbo and Hui, with General of the Guard Yuan Can, plotted at Stone citadel; Hui sent Houbo's light boats downriver, but the armies were already there and they could not get in.

sentences.zh: 太祖令安國至鎮，收候伯誅之。

translations.literal: The Founder ordered Anguo to his post, seized Houbo and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent Anguo to his command, seized Houbo, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 尋進號前將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to General of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was raised to General of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: ，進爵，增邑六百戶。

translations.literal: , he advanced in rank, fief increased by six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised in rank and his fief grew by six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉右衞將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard, with added offering attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to General of the Right Guard with added offering attendant.

sentences.zh: 二年，虜寇邊，上遣安國出司州，安集民戶。

translations.literal: In the second year the northerners raided the border; the emperor sent Anguo out to Si Province to settle the people and households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the northern enemy struck the border; the throne sent Anguo into Si to settle the people.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「郢、司之閒，流雜繁廣，宜竝加區判，定其隷屬。

translations.literal: An edict said: 「Between Ying and Si, dispersed settlers are many and broad; they should all be marked off by district and their subordination fixed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 「Between Ying and Si the displaced are many and scattered; they should be sorted by district and their allegiance fixed.

sentences.zh: 參詳兩州，事無專任，安國可蹔往經理。

translations.literal: Review both provinces; no one bears sole charge—Anguo may go temporarily to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: Look to both provinces: no one holds sole charge—Anguo may go for a time to put things in order.

sentences.zh: 」以本官使持節、總荊郢諸軍北討事，屯義陽西關。

translations.literal: 」With his existing rank, envoy with credentials, overall commander of Jing and Ying military affairs for the northern campaign, encamped at Yiyang's western pass.
translations.idiomatic: 」At his present rank he was made envoy with credentials, overall commander of Jing and Ying for the northern campaign, and camped at Yiyang's western pass.

sentences.zh: 虜未至，安國移屯沔口以俟應接。

translations.literal: The enemy did not come; Anguo moved his camp to the Mian mouth to await support.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy never came; Anguo shifted camp to the mouth of the Mian to stand ready for relief.

sentences.zh: 改封湘郷。

translations.literal: He was re-enfeoffed at Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed at Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，授使持節、散騎常侍、平西將軍、司州刺史，領義陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he was granted envoy with credentials, supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, inspector of Si Province, still administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne he received credentials as envoy, supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, and inspector of Si, still holding Yiyang as administrator.

sentences.zh: ，徙都督南兖兖徐青冀五州諸軍事、平北將軍、南兖州刺史，仍爲都督、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: , he was moved to oversee South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of South Yan; still overseer and inspector of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made overseer of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of South Yan, while still overseeing Xiang as inspector.

sentences.zh: 四年，湘川蠻動，安國督州兵討之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Xiangxiang barbarians stirred; Anguo oversaw provincial troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the tribes of Xiang rose; Anguo led provincial troops to put them down.

sentences.zh: 有疾，徵爲光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He fell ill and was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Illness brought him to court as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 安國欣有文授，謂其子曰：「汝後勿作褶驅使，單衣猶恨不稱，當爲朱衣官也。

translations.literal: Anguo delighted that he had literary learning for his sons; he told his son: 「After me do not become a pleated-coat driver; plain dress still seems not fitting—you should be a vermilion-robed official.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo rejoiced that his sons had learning; he told his son: 「Hereafter do not serve as a pleated-coat driver—even plain robes still feel unworthy; you should wear vermilion and hold office.

sentences.zh: 」上遣中書舍人茹法亮敕安國曰：「吾恒憂卿疾病，應有所須，勿致難也。

translations.literal: 」The emperor sent Secretarial Attendant Ru Faliang to instruct Anguo: 「I constantly worry over your illness; should you need anything, do not make it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor sent Secretarial Attendant Ru Faliang to tell Anguo: 「I always fret over your sickness; if you need anything, do not hold back.

sentences.zh: 」明年，遷都官尚書，領太子左率。

translations.literal: 」The next year he was moved to Minister of Justice, leading the crown prince's left guard.
translations.idiomatic: 」The next year he was made minister of justice and led the crown prince's left guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷領軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to General of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made General of the Army.

sentences.zh: 安國累居將率，在朝以宿舊見遇。

translations.literal: Anguo long held command ranks; in court he was treated as an elder of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo had long stood at the head of armies; at court he was honored as an old companion.

sentences.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫、兖州中正，給扶。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, Household Minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, impartial nominee for Yan Province, with support staff provided.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was raised to supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, household minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, and impartial nominee for Yan, with attendants to lean on.

sentences.zh: 上又敕茹法亮曰：「吾見呂安國疾狀，自不宜勞，且脚中旣恒惡，扶人至吾前，於禮望殊成有虧，吾難敕之。

translations.literal: The emperor again instructed Ru Faliang: 「I have seen Lu Anguo's medical reports—by himself he is unfit for labor; moreover his feet have long been bad, and to be helped before me is a great loss to ceremonial bearing; I find it hard to order him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again told Ru Faliang: 「I have read Lu Anguo's medical notes—he is plainly unfit for exertion; his feet have long troubled him, and to be led before me would shame his standing in ritual; I cannot bring myself to command it.

sentences.zh: 其人甚諱病，卿可作私意向，其若好差不復須扶人，依例入，幸勿牽勉。

translations.literal: The man greatly hides his illness; you may make a private inquiry—if he is somewhat better and no longer needs support, let him enter by precedent; do not press him.
translations.idiomatic: He hides his sickness deeply; speak to him privately—if he improves enough to walk unaided, let him come in as usual; do not force him.

sentences.zh: 」八年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: 」In the eighth year he died, at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: 」In the eighth year he died, at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、鎮北將軍、南兖州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted envoy with credentials, General Who Guards the North, inspector of South Yan Province, attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted credentials as envoy, General Who Guards the North, and inspector of South Yan, with attendant rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Given one set of martial music instruments.
translations.idiomatic: He was given one suite of martial music.

sentences.zh: 諡肅侯。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 全景文

translations.literal: Quan Jingwen
translations.idiomatic: Quan Jingwen

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 時舊將帥又有吳郡全景文，字弘達。

translations.literal: At the time among veteran commanders there was also Quan Jingwen of Wu commandery, styled Hongda.
translations.idiomatic: Among the old guard of that age was Quan Jingwen of Wu, styled Hongda.

sentences.zh: 少有氣力，與沈攸之同載出都，到奔牛埭，於岸上息，有人相之：「君等皆方伯人，行當富貴也。

translations.literal: In youth he had strength and spirit; he left the capital in the same carriage as Shen Youzhi. At Beniu Ford they rested on the bank, and a man read their fortunes: "You are both men destined for regional command; wealth and rank lie ahead."
translations.idiomatic: Young and full of vigor, he rode out of the capital with Shen Youzhi in the same carriage. At Beniu Ford they rested on the embankment, and a fortune-teller told them, "You are both men fated for regional command—riches and rank await."

sentences.zh: 」景文謂攸之曰：「富貴或可一人耳，今言皆然，此殆妄言也。

translations.literal: Jingwen said to Youzhi: "Fortune might come to one of us alone; now he says we both will—this is likely idle talk."
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen said to Youzhi, "Wealth may fall to one man alone; now he says we both shall have it—this is probably empty talk."

sentences.zh: 」景文仍得將領爲軍主。

translations.literal: Jingwen nevertheless obtained a command and became an army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen still won a command and served as an army chief.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，爲竟陵王驃騎行參軍，以功封漢水侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian, he served as adjutant on the Prince of Jingling's Rapid Cavalry staff and, for merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hanshui.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiaojian reign he was adjutant on the Prince of Jingling's rapid-cavalry staff and, for merit, enfeoffed Marquis of Hanshui.

sentences.zh: 除員外郎，積射將軍。

translations.literal: He was made an outer court gentleman and General Who Shoots with Vigor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an outer court gentleman and general who shoots with vigor.

sentences.zh: ，爲假節、寧朔將軍、冗從僕射、軍主。

translations.literal: He was also made bearer of credentials, General Who Pacifies the North, Vice Director of the Imperial Bodyguard, and army commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made bearer of credentials, general who pacifies the north, vice director of the imperial bodyguard, and army commander.

sentences.zh: 隨前將軍劉亮討破東賊於晉陵，除長水校尉，假輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the vanguard general Liu Liang in crushing eastern rebels at Jinling and was made Colonel of the Chang River, acting General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the vanguard general Liu Liang in crushing eastern rebels at Jinling and was made colonel of the Chang River, acting general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 北討薛索兒於破釜，領水軍斷賊糧運。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign against Xue Suo'er at Pofu, he led the water forces and cut the rebels' grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning north against Xue Suo'er at Pofu, he led the river fleet and severed the rebels' grain route.

sentences.zh: 仍隨太祖於葛冢石梁，再戰皆有功。

translations.literal: He then followed the Founding Emperor at Ge Mound and Shiliang, distinguishing himself in both battles.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed the founding emperor at Ge Mound and Shiliang and distinguished himself in both fights.

sentences.zh: 南賊相持未決，敕景文隷劉亮拒劉胡，攻圍力戰，身被數十創，除前軍將軍，封孝寧縣侯，邑六百戶。

translations.literal: While southern rebels held the field unresolved, an edict ordered Jingwen under Liu Liang to hold off Liu Hu; in assault and siege he fought fiercely, suffering dozens of wounds, and was made General of the Vanguard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiaoning with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: While southern rebels still held the field, an edict placed Jingwen under Liu Liang to block Liu Hu; in assault and siege he fought until he bore dozens of wounds, then was made general of the vanguard and enfeoffed Marquis of Xiaoning at six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除寧朔將軍，游擊將軍，假輔師將軍，高平太守，鎮軍、安西二府司馬，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the North, General Who Roams and Strikes, acting General Who Assists the Army, Administrator of Gaoping, staff officer to the Pacifying the Army and Pacifying the West headquarters, and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the north, general who roams and strikes, acting general who assists the army, administrator of Gaoping, staff officer to the pacifying-the-army and pacifying-the-west headquarters, and general of valiant cavalry.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，出爲南豫州刺史、歷陽太守，輔國將軍如故。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui he went out as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou and Administrator of Liyang, retaining his rank as General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhui reign he went out as inspector of southern Yuzhou and administrator of Liyang, keeping his rank as general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 遷征虜將軍、南琅邪濟陰二郡太守、軍主，尋加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General Who Captures the Barbarians, Administrator of the two commanderies of Southern Langye and Jiyin, and army commander; soon after he was given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who captures the barbarians, administrator of southern Langye and Jiyin, and army chief, and soon after was given regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，以不預佐命，國除，授南琅邪太守，常侍、將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, because he had not taken part in the founding enterprise, his state was abolished; he was appointed Administrator of Southern Langye, retaining his attendant and general titles.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 1, because he had not shared in the founding enterprise, his marquisate was abolished; he was made administrator of southern Langye, attendant and general titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫，征虜將軍、臨川王征西司馬、南郡太守。

translations.literal: He was moved to Household Minister of the Glory of State, General Who Captures the Barbarians, western campaign staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made household minister of the glory of state, general who captures the barbarians, western-campaign staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan, and administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 還，累遷爲給事中，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he rose step by step to Supervisor within the Gates and Household Minister of the Glory of State.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he rose by stages to supervisor within the gates and household minister of the glory of state.

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 周山圖

translations.literal: Zhou Shantu
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shantu

sentences.zh: 周山圖字季寂，義興義郷人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Shantu, styled Jiji, was a native of Yixiang in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shantu, styled Jiji, came from Yixiang in Yixing.

sentences.zh: 少貧微，傭書自業。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and lowly and hired himself out copying books for a living.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was poor and copied books for hire to earn his bread.

sentences.zh: 有氣幹，爲吳郡晉陵防郡隊主。

translations.literal: He had force and resolve and became chief of a defense district squad in Jinling, Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He had grit and backbone and became chief of a frontier-defense squad in Jinling, Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武伐太初，山圖豫勳，賜爵關中侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Song campaigned against Taichu, Shantu shared in the merit and was given the title Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Song marched against Taichu, Shantu shared in the merit and was enfeoffed marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 兖州刺史沈僧榮鎮瑕丘，與山圖有舊，以爲己建武府參軍。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Shen Rongrong held Xiaqiu and, having old ties with Shantu, took him as adjutant on his Jianwu headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou inspector Shen Rongrong held Xiaqiu; knowing Shantu of old, he made him adjutant on his Jianwu staff.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵反，僧榮遣山圖領二百人詣沈慶之受節度，事平論勳，爲中書舍人戴明寶所抑。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jingling, Dan, seized Guangling in revolt, Rongrong sent Shantu with two hundred men to Shen Qingzhi to take his orders; when affairs were settled and merit was reckoned, he was held back by Palace Attendant Dai Mingbao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingling, Dan, held Guangling in revolt, Rongrong sent Shantu with two hundred men to Shen Qingzhi for orders; when the revolt was crushed and merit was tallied, palace attendant Dai Mingbao blocked his reward.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，爲殿中將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was made a palace guard general.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taishi reign he was made a palace guard general.

sentences.zh: 四方反叛，僕射王彧舉山圖將領，呼與語，甚悅，使領百舸爲前驅。

translations.literal: When the four quarters rebelled, Vice Director Wang Yu recommended Shantu for command; the emperor called him in to speak and was much pleased, and had him lead a hundred war-boats as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion flared on every side, vice director Wang Yu put forward Shantu; the emperor summoned him, took great pleasure in their talk, and set him at the head of a hundred war-boats.

sentences.zh: 與軍主佼長生等攻破賊湖白、赭圻二城。

translations.literal: With the army commander Jiao Changsheng and others he stormed the rebel strongholds of Hubai and Zheqi.
translations.idiomatic: With the army chief Jiao Changsheng and others he stormed the rebel towns of Hubai and Zheqi.

sentences.zh: 除員外郎，加振武將軍。

translations.literal: He was made outer court gentleman and given the additional rank of General Who Quakes the Foe.
translations.idiomatic: He was made outer court gentleman with the added rank of general who quakes the foe.

sentences.zh: 豫平濃湖，追賊至西陽還，明帝賞之，賜苑西宅一區。

translations.literal: He took part in pacifying Nong Lake; pursuing the enemy to Xiyang and returning, Emperor Ming rewarded him with one residence in the western park quarter.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify Nong Lake, pursued the rebels to Xiyang, and on his return Emperor Ming rewarded him with a house in the western park quarter.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍張永征薛安都於彭城，山圖領二千人迎運至武原，爲虜騎所追，合戰，多所傷殺。

translations.literal: When Pacifying the Army General Zhang Yong campaigned against Xue Andu at Pengcheng, Shantu led two thousand men to meet the supply convoy at Wuyuan; pursued by barbarian horsemen, he joined battle and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: When pacifying-the-army general Zhang Yong marched on Xue Andu at Pengcheng, Shantu led two thousand men to meet the supply train at Wuyuan; northern horsemen overtook him, and in the clash many fell.

sentences.zh: 虜圍轉急，山圖據城自固，然後更結陣死戰，突圍出，虜披靡不能禁。

translations.literal: As the encirclement tightened, Shantu held the city fast, then re-formed his ranks for a death fight, broke out, and the enemy scattered before him, unable to check him.
translations.idiomatic: As the ring closed tighter, Shantu held the town fast, then re-formed his ranks for a death fight, broke out, and the enemy broke before him and could not hold him.

sentences.zh: 衆稱其勇，呼爲「武原將」。

translations.literal: The troops praised his bravery and called him "the General of Wuyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The men praised his courage and named him the General of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 及永軍大敗，山圖收散卒得千餘人，守下邳城。

translations.literal: When Yong's army suffered a great defeat, Shantu gathered the scattered soldiers, mustered more than a thousand, and held Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong's army was routed, Shantu gathered the fugitives, mustered more than a thousand men, and held Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 還除給事中、冗從僕射、直閤將軍。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Supervisor within the Gates, Vice Director of the Imperial Bodyguard, and General of the Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made supervisor within the gates, vice director of the imperial bodyguard, and general of the direct guard.

sentences.zh: 山圖好酒多失，明帝數加怒誚，後遂自改。

translations.literal: Shantu drank heavily and often fell short; Emperor Ming repeatedly rebuked him in anger, and afterward he reformed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu drank hard and often failed in duty; Emperor Ming rebuked him again and again, until at last he mended his ways.

sentences.zh: 出爲錢唐新城戍。

translations.literal: He went out to garrison the new city of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to garrison the new town of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 是時豫州淮西地新沒虜，更於歷陽立鎮，五年，以山圖爲龍驤將軍、歷陽令，領兵守城。

translations.literal: At that time the Huai west country of Yuzhou had newly fallen to the northerners, and a garrison was re-established at Liyang; in the fifth year Shantu was made General of Lofty Dragon, Magistrate of Liyang, and led troops to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai-west lands of Yuzhou had just been lost to the north, and a new garrison was set at Liyang; in the fifth year Shantu was made general of lofty dragon and magistrate of Liyang, with troops to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 初，臨海亡命田流，自號「東海王」，逃竄會稽鄞縣邊海山谷中，立屯營，分布要害，官軍不能討。

translations.literal: Earlier, the fugitive Tian Liu of Linhai styled himself "King of the Eastern Sea," lurking in the mountain valleys along the coast of Yin county in Kuaiji, setting up camps and holding key points so that government forces could not suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Linhai outlaw, Tian Liu, styled himself King of the Eastern Sea and hid in the coastal hills of Yin in Kuaiji, building camps and seizing choke points so that government troops could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣直後聞人襲說降之，授流龍驤將軍，流受命，將黨與出，行達海鹽，放兵大掠而反。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent the palace attendant Wenren Xi to persuade him to surrender and invested Liu as General of Lofty Dragon; Liu accepted, led his followers out, and upon reaching Haiyan let his soldiers loose in great pillage and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent the palace attendant Wenren Xi to offer surrender and made Liu general of lofty dragon; Liu accepted, marched his band out, and at Haiyan loosed them in wide plunder and turned back.

sentences.zh: 是冬，殺鄞令耿猷，東境大震。

translations.literal: That winter he killed the magistrate of Yin, Geng You, and the eastern border was thrown into alarm.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he killed Yin magistrate Geng You, and the eastern frontier shook.

sentences.zh: 六年，敕山圖將兵東屯浹口，廣設購募。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict ordered Shantu to take troops east and encamp at Jia Mouth, with broad offers of reward for enlistment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict sent Shantu east with troops to camp at Jia Mouth and posted lavish rewards for heads.

sentences.zh: 流爲其副暨挐所殺，別帥杜連、梅洛生各擁衆自守。

translations.literal: Liu was killed by his lieutenant Ji Nuo; the separate chieftains Du Lian and Mei Luosheng each held their own followers in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was killed by his lieutenant Ji Nuo; the chieftains Du Lian and Mei Luosheng each kept their own bands under arms.

sentences.zh: 至明年，山圖分兵掩討，皆平之。

translations.literal: By the next year Shantu divided his forces for sudden strikes and subdued them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shantu split his forces for surprise attacks and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 豫章賊張鳳，聚衆康樂山，斷江劫抄。

translations.literal: The rebel Zhang Feng of Yuzhang gathered a host on Mt. Kangle, blocked the river, and plundered passing craft.
translations.idiomatic: A Yuzhang rebel, Zhang Feng, gathered men on Mt. Kangle, blocked the river, and robbed passing boats.

sentences.zh: 臺軍主李雙、蔡保數遣軍攻之，連年不禽。

translations.literal: The central army commanders Li Shuang and Cai Bao sent troops against him repeatedly for years without taking him.
translations.idiomatic: Central commanders Li Shuang and Cai Bao sent troops against him year after year and could not take him.

sentences.zh: 至是軍主毛寄生與鳳戰於豫章江，大敗。

translations.literal: On this occasion the army commander Mao Jisheng fought Feng on the Zhang river and suffered a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Now the army chief Mao Jisheng met Feng on the Zhang River and was routed.

sentences.zh: 明帝復遣山圖討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming again sent Shantu to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming again sent Shantu against him.

sentences.zh: 山圖至，先羸兵偃衆，遣幢主龐嗣厚遺鳳，要出會聚，聽以兵自衞，鳳信之。

translations.literal: When Shantu arrived, he first hid his strength and feigned weakness, then sent his banner commander Pang Si with lavish gifts to Feng, inviting him to a meeting and allowing him to bring an armed escort; Feng believed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shantu arrived, he first thinned his ranks and played weakness, then sent his banner chief Pang Si with rich gifts to Feng, asking him to a meeting and letting him bring guards; Feng trusted him.

sentences.zh: 行至望蔡，山圖設伏兵於水側，擊斬鳳首，衆百餘人束首降。

translations.literal: When he reached Wangcai, Shantu set ambush troops beside the water, struck and killed Feng Shou, and more than a hundred men bound their heads and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Wangcai, Shantu laid an ambush along the waterline, cut down Feng Shou, and took the surrender of a hundred-odd men who came forward bound.

sentences.zh: 除寧朔將軍、漣口戍主。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the North and garrison commander of Lian Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and put in charge of the Lian Mouth garrison.

sentences.zh: 山圖遏漣水築西城，斷虜騎路，并以溉田。

translations.literal: Shantu dammed the Lian River to build West City, cutting the northerners' cavalry route and also irrigating the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu checked the Lian River to raise West City, blocking the northerners' horse-road and opening the water to the fields besides.

sentences.zh: ，遷步兵校尉，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: , He was moved to Colonel of Foot Soldiers, with the added rank of General Who Establishes Martial Prowess.
translations.idiomatic: He was then shifted to Colonel of Foot Soldiers, with the added title General Who Establishes Martial Prowess.

sentences.zh: 轉督高平下邳淮陽淮西四郡諸軍事、寧朔將軍、淮南太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to oversee military affairs of the four commanderies Gao Ping, Xiapi, Huaiyang, and Huai West, as General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was turned to command the armies of Gao Ping, Xiapi, Huaiyang, and Huai West, still as General Who Pacifies the North and now as administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 盜發桓溫塚，大獲寶物。

translations.literal: Tomb robbers opened Huan Wen's grave and obtained a great store of treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Grave robbers broke into Huan Wen's tomb and carried off a vast hoard of treasure.

sentences.zh: 客竊取以遺山圖，山圖不受，簿以還官。

translations.literal: A guest stole some and offered them to Shantu; Shantu would not accept them and registered them to return to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: A guest stole a portion and tried to give it to Shantu; Shantu refused the gift and entered every piece in the ledger for return to the state.

sentences.zh: 遷左中郎將。

translations.literal: He was moved to Left Leader of the Palace Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Leader of the Palace Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，山圖密啓曰：「沈攸之久有異圖，公宜深爲之備。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor assisted in government, Shantu secretly memorialized: 「Shen Youzhi has long harbored contrary designs; my lord should prepare against him in depth.
translations.idiomatic: While the Grand Ancestor held the reins, Shantu sent a secret memorial: 「Shen Youzhi has nursed disloyal designs for years; you should arm yourself against him to the full.

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑而納之。

translations.literal: 」The Grand Ancestor smiled and took it in.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Grand Ancestor smiled and accepted the warning.

sentences.zh: 武陵王贊爲郢州，太祖令山圖領兵衞送。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling, Zan, went out to Ying Province, the Grand Ancestor ordered Shantu to lead troops on the escort guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling, Zan, took up Ying Province, the Grand Ancestor set Shantu at the head of the guard that saw him there.

sentences.zh: 世祖與晉熙王燮自郢下，以山圖爲後防。

translations.literal: The Shizu emperor and the Prince of Jinxi, Xie, came down from Ying, with Shantu as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu emperor and the Prince of Jinxi, Xie, marched down from Ying with Shantu holding the rear.

sentences.zh: 攸之事起，世祖爲西討都督，啓山圖爲軍副。

translations.literal: When Youzhi's revolt broke out, Shizu was western campaign overseer and recommended Shantu as army deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Once Youzhi rose, Shizu took the western command and had Shantu named his army deputy.

sentences.zh: 世祖留據盆城，衆議以盆城城小難固，不如還都。

translations.literal: Shizu held at Pencheng; the assembly argued that Pencheng was small and hard to hold, and that it would be better to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu stayed to hold Pencheng. The council held that the town was too small to stand a siege and urged a return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 山圖曰：「今據中流，爲四方勢援，大衆致力，川岳可爲。

translations.literal: Shantu said: 「We now hold the midstream as a buttress for forces on every side; if the great host joins its strength, rivers and mountains can be made to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu said: 「We sit on the river's spine, a brace for every quarter. Let the mass of men bend their strength together, and stream and ridge become our rampart.

sentences.zh: 城隍小事，不足難也。

translations.literal: City walls and moats are small matters—not enough to be a difficulty.」
translations.idiomatic: Walls and ditches are trifles; they are not what should stop us.」

sentences.zh: 」世祖使城局參軍劉皆、陳淵委山圖以處分事。

translations.literal: Shizu had the city bureau staff officers Liu Jie and Chen Yuan entrust Shantu with the disposition of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu put Liu Jie and Chen Yuan of the city bureau under orders to leave all arrangements to Shantu.

sentences.zh: 山圖斷取行旅船板，以造樓櫓，立水柵，旬日皆辦。

translations.literal: Shantu took planks from travelers' boats to build siege towers and water palisades; within ten days all was ready.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu stripped passing boats for timber, raised fighting towers and a water fence, and had the whole work finished inside ten days.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Shizu greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 授前軍將軍，加寧朔將軍，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was granted Front Army General, with added rank as General Who Pacifies the North, and his title advanced to General Who Aids the State.
translations.idiomatic: He received Front Army General, kept Pacifies the North as an added rank, and was raised to General Who Aids the State.

sentences.zh: 攸之攻郢城，世祖令山圖量其形勢。

translations.literal: Youzhi attacked Ying city; Shizu had Shantu assess the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi laid siege to Ying, Shizu asked Shantu to read the field.

sentences.zh: 山圖曰：「攸之見與隣郷，亟同征伐，悉其爲人。

translations.literal: Shantu said: 「Youzhi and I grew up as neighbors and campaigned together again and again—I know the man.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu said: 「Youzhi and I were boys from the same country, and we have marched together time after time. I know him through and through.

sentences.zh: 性度險刻，無以結固士心。

translations.literal: His nature is harsh and cutting; he cannot bind his men's hearts firm.
translations.idiomatic: He is narrow and cruel by temper, and has no gift for winning soldiers to stand fast.

sentences.zh: 如頓兵堅城之下，適所以爲離散之漸耳。

translations.literal: To camp his army under a strong wall is precisely to give his men the first step toward scattering.」
translations.idiomatic: Let him sit his host beneath stout walls, and he will only teach them how to drift apart.」

sentences.zh: 」攸之旣敗，平西將軍黃回乘輕舸從白服百餘人在軍前下緣流呌，盆城中恐，須臾知是回凱歸，乃安。

translations.literal: When Youzhi was beaten, General Who Pacifies the West Huang Hui took a light skiff with more than a hundred men in white garb and came shouting down along the stream before the army; Pencheng was terrified, then in a moment knew it was Hui returning in triumph and was calmed.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhi's defeat, Huang Hui, General Who Pacifies the West, came downriver in a light boat with a hundred-odd men in white, calling from the bow. Pencheng took them for the enemy and shook with fear—then, in a breath, saw it was Hui home in victory, and steadied.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂山圖曰：「周公前言，可謂明於見事矣。

translations.literal: Shizu said to Shantu: 「Duke Zhou, your earlier words may be called clear sight in reading events.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu told Shantu: 「Your earlier words, Duke Zhou, were foresight plain to see.

sentences.zh: 」還都，太祖遣山圖領部曲，鎮京城，鎮戍諸軍，悉受節度。

translations.literal: 」On returning to the capital, the Grand Ancestor sent Shantu to lead his personal troops and garrison the capital; all garrison armies were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: 」Back in the capital, the Grand Ancestor set Shantu at the head of his household troops to hold the city; every garrison force fell under his orders.

sentences.zh: 遷游擊將軍，輔國如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to Mobile-Strike General; his rank as Aids the State stood unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Mobile-Strike General, still General Who Aids the State as before.

sentences.zh: ，封廣晉縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: , He was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangjin county, with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangjin, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 出爲假節、督兖青冀三州徐州東海朐山軍事、寧朔將軍、兖州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out with acting credentials as overseer of military affairs in Yan, Qing, and Ji, and in Xu's Donghai and Qushan, as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearing acting credentials to command Yan, Qing, and Ji and Xu's Donghai and Qushan, as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 百姓附之。

translations.literal: The common people attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 二年，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year his title advanced to General Who Aids the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was raised to General Who Aids the State.

sentences.zh: 其秋，虜動，上策虜必不出淮陰，乃敕山圖曰：「知卿綏邊撫戎，甚有次第，應變算略，悉以相委。

translations.literal: That autumn the northerners stirred; the emperor judged they would certainly not come out of Huaiyin, and charged Shantu: 「I know you pacify the border and comfort the troops in good order; every plan for meeting change I place wholly in your hands.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the northerners moved. The throne reckoned they would not dare break from Huaiyin and wrote to Shantu: 「I know you steady the frontier and keep the army in hand, step by step. Every turn of the fight I leave to you.

sentences.zh: 恐列醜未必能送死，卿丈夫無可藉手耳。

translations.literal: I fear the ranks of uglies may not all come to die for it—my good man, there is nothing else to lean on.」
translations.idiomatic: I doubt every savage in their columns will rush to their deaths—husband, I have no other hand to grasp.」

sentences.zh: 」虜果寇朐山，爲玄元度、盧紹之所破。

translations.literal: The northerners did raid Qushan and were broken by Xuan Yuandu and Lu Shaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners struck Qushan as foretold and were shattered by Xuan Yuandu and Lu Shaozhi.

sentences.zh: 虜於淮陽。

translations.literal: The northerners were at Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: They were at Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 是時淮北四州起義，上使山圖自淮入清，倍道應赴。

translations.literal: At that time the four Huai-north provinces rose in loyalty; the emperor sent Shantu from the Huai into Qing by forced marches to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the four provinces north of the Huai rose for the throne. The emperor ordered Shantu in from the Huai toward Qing at double pace.

sentences.zh: 敕山圖曰：「卿當盡相帥馭理，每存全重，天下事，唯同心力，山岳可摧。

translations.literal: An edict to Shantu said: 「You must lead and govern to the full, always keeping the weight whole; under heaven, only if hearts join their strength can mountains crumble.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Shantu again: 「Lead every man you command and keep the whole body intact. Under heaven, only when all hearts pull one way can mountains be thrown down.

sentences.zh: 然用兵當使背後無憂慮；

translations.literal: Yet in using troops one must leave no worry behind one's back;
translations.idiomatic: Yet war wants a rear with nothing left to fear;

sentences.zh: 若後冷然無橫來處，閉目痛打，無不摧碎。

translations.literal: if the rear is calm with no assault from the side, close your eyes and strike hard—nothing will fail to shatter.
translations.idiomatic: if your back stays cold and no blow comes across it, shut your eyes and hit with all you have—nothing you strike will stand.

sentences.zh: 吾政應鑄金，待卿成勳耳。

translations.literal: I ought to cast you in gold and wait for your achievement.」
translations.idiomatic: I should be casting you in gold, waiting on the deed you bring home.」

sentences.zh: 若不藉此平四州，非丈夫也。

translations.literal: If you do not use this to pacify the four provinces, you are no true man.
translations.idiomatic: Fail to take this chance and settle the four provinces, and you are no man worth the name.

sentences.zh: 努力自運，勿令他人得上功。

translations.literal: Strive on your own account—do not let another man take the top credit.」
translations.idiomatic: Drive yourself—do not let another wear the first laurel.」

sentences.zh: 」會義衆已爲虜所沒，山圖拔三百家還淮陰。

translations.literal: But the righteous hosts had already been swallowed by the northerners; Shantu drew out three hundred households back to Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: By then the loyalist bands had already been overrun. Shantu pulled three hundred families back to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 表移東海郡治漣口，又於石鼈立陽平郡，皆見納。

translations.literal: He memorialized moving the seat of Donghai commandery to Lian Mouth and establishing Yangping commandery at Shibie; both proposals were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to move Donghai's seat to Lian Mouth and to set up Yangping commandery at Shibie; the court accepted both.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，遷竟陵王鎮北司馬，帶南平昌太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Shantu was moved to staff of the north garrison for the Prince of Jingling, with concurrent office as administrator of Nan Pingchang; his generalships stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession, Shantu became staff of the Prince of Jingling's northern garrison, with Nan Pingchang added under his charge; his general's titles were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以盆城之舊，出入殿省，甚見親信。

translations.literal: For old ties at Pencheng, he moved in and out of the palace offices and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of their days at Pencheng, he passed freely through the palace offices and stood high in favor.

sentences.zh: 義郷縣長風廟神姓鄧，先經爲縣令，死遂發靈。

translations.literal: In Yixiang, the god of Changfeng Temple, surnamed Deng, had once served as magistrate; after death his spirit was aroused.
translations.idiomatic: At Yixiang the god of Changfeng Temple bore the surname Deng and had once been magistrate; when he died, his spirit began to answer.

sentences.zh: 山圖啓乞加神位輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Shantu memorialized asking that the god be given the rank General Who Aids the State.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu asked leave to grant the god the rank General Who Aids the State.

sentences.zh: 上答曰：「足狗肉便了事，何用階級爲？

translations.literal: The emperor answered: 「Dog meat alone would settle it—what need for ranks and grades?
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: 「A plate of dog meat would finish the business—why trouble over ranks and grades?

sentences.zh: 」轉黃門郎，領羽林四廂直衞。

translations.literal: 」He was transferred to gentleman of the yellow gate and led the direct guard of the four wings of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was made gentleman of the yellow gate and put in charge of the Feathered Forest's four direct-guard wings.

sentences.zh: 山圖於新林立墅舍，晨夜往還。

translations.literal: Shantu built a villa at Xinlin and went back and forth morning and night.
translations.idiomatic: Shantu raised a country house at Xinlin and traveled there and back from dawn to dark.

sentences.zh: 上謂之曰：「卿罷萬人都督，而輕行郊外。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: 「You have left your post as commander of ten thousand, yet still travel lightly in the outskirts.
translations.idiomatic: The throne told him: 「You have given up command of ten thousand men, yet you still ride out lightly into the open country.

sentences.zh: 自今往墅，可以仗身自隨，以備不虞。

translations.literal: From now on, when you go to the villa, you may take armed bodyguards with you against the unforeseen.」
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, when you go to the villa, take armed attendants with you, against whatever may come.」

sentences.zh: 」及疾，上手敕參問，遣醫給藥。

translations.literal: 」When he fell ill, the emperor wrote in his own hand to inquire after him and sent physicians with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: 」When illness took him, the throne wrote in its own hand to ask after him and sent doctors with medicine.

sentences.zh: ，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: , and he died at sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 詔賜朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: An edict granted one set of court dress and one suit of garments.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gave him one court robe and one suit of clothes.

sentences.zh: 周盤龍

translations.literal: Zhou Panlong
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Panlong

sentences.zh: 周盤龍，北蘭陵蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Panlong was a man of Lanling in North Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Panlong came from Lanling in North Lanling.

sentences.zh: 宋世土斷，屬東平郡。

translations.literal: Under the Song land-allotment reforms he was attached to Dongping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song redrew native registers, his household was placed in Dongping commandery.

sentences.zh: 盤龍膽氣過人，尤便弓馬。

translations.literal: Panlong's courage outstripped other men; he was especially skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's nerve outstripped other men, and he was most at home with bow and saddle.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，隨軍討赭圻賊，躬自鬬戰，陷陣先登。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he followed the army against the Zhexi rebels, fought in person in the melee, broke the line, and was first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi he marched against the Zhexi rebels, fought hand to hand in the press, broke the enemy line, and was first up the wall.

sentences.zh: 累至龍驤將軍、積射將軍，封晉安縣子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to Dragon-soaring General and Volley General, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jin'an with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed by stages to Dragon-soaring General and Volley General and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jin'an with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: ，桂陽賊起，盤龍時爲冗從僕射、騎官主、領馬軍主，隨太祖頓新亭，與屯騎校尉黃回出城南，與賊對陣，尋引還城中，合力拒戰。

translations.literal: , when the Guiyang rebels rose, Panlong was then supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, master of the horse guards, and commanding the horse army; he followed the Grand Ancestor in holding Xinting, and with Colonel of the Martial Riders Huang Hui went out south of the city to face the rebels in battle, then drew back into the city and joined forces to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guiyang rebels rose, Panlong was supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, master of the horse guards, and horse-army commander. He followed the Grand Ancestor to hold Xinting, went out south of the wall with Colonel of the Martial Riders Huang Hui to meet the rebels in line, then pulled back inside the city and fought shoulder to shoulder with the rest.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除南東莞太守，加前軍將軍，稍至驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was made administrator of South Dongguan, with added rank as Vanguard General, and gradually reached General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace returned, he was named administrator of South Dongguan and Vanguard General, and in time rose to General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: ，出爲假節、督交廣二州軍事、征虜將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，未之官，預平石頭。

translations.literal: , he went out with acting credentials as overseer of military affairs in Jiao and Guang, General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guang; before he took up the post he took part in pacifying Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out with acting credentials to oversee Jiao and Guang, as General Who Punishes the Barbarians, Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guang. Before he reached his post he helped take Shitou.

sentences.zh: 二年，沈攸之平，司州刺史姚道和懷貳被徵，以盤龍督司州軍事、司州刺史、假節，將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the second year Shen Youzhi was pacified; Inspector of Si Yao Daodao harbored divided loyalties and was recalled; Panlong was made overseer of Si military affairs, Inspector of Si, with acting credentials; his general's rank stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, with Shen Youzhi put down, Inspector of Si Yao Daodao was recalled for divided loyalties. Panlong was put in charge of Si as overseer of its armies and inspector, with acting credentials; his general's rank was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 改封沌陽縣。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Dunyang county.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was shifted to Dunyang county.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，進號右將軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, his title advanced to General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Ancestor's accession his rank rose to General of the Right.

sentences.zh: ，虜寇壽春，以盤龍爲軍主、假節，助豫州刺史垣崇祖決水漂漬。

translations.literal: , the northerners raided Shouchun; Panlong was made army commander with acting credentials to aid Inspector of Yu Yuan Chongzu in breaking the dikes and flooding them.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners struck Shouchun. Panlong was named army commander with acting credentials to help Inspector of Yu Yuan Chongzu breach the dikes and drown the enemy camps.

sentences.zh: 盤龍率輔國將軍張倪馬步軍於西澤中奮擊，殺傷數萬人，獲牛馬輜重。

translations.literal: Panlong led the mixed horse and foot of Supporting-the-State General Zhang Ni in a fierce attack in the western marsh, killing and wounding tens of thousands, and capturing cattle, horses, and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong drove the horse-and-foot columns of Supporting-the-State General Zhang Ni in a furious strike through the western marsh, killing and wounding tens of thousands and taking cattle, horses, and supply trains.

sentences.zh: 上聞之喜，詔曰：「醜虜送死，敢寇壽春，崇祖、盤龍正勒義勇，乘機電奮，水陸斬擊，填川蔽野。

translations.literal: The emperor heard with delight and issued an edict: 「The vile northerners court death, daring to raid Shouchun. Chongzu and Panlong are just now mustering the volunteers, seizing the moment with lightning zeal, cutting them down on water and land until the valleys are filled and the plains are hidden.
translations.idiomatic: The throne heard and rejoiced, then issued an edict: 「The foul northerners come seeking death, daring to strike Shouchun. Chongzu and Panlong are even now steeling the loyal and brave, riding the moment like lightning, cutting them down on river and road until gullies brim and fields go dark with the slain.

sentences.zh: 師不淹晨，西蕃剋定。

translations.literal: The army did not linger past morning; the western borderlands were taken in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: The host did not wait out the morning; the western frontier was settled in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 斯實將率用命之功，文武爭伐之力。

translations.literal: This is truly the merit of commanders who give their all, and the strength of civil and martial men contending in prowess.
translations.idiomatic: This is the work of generals who spent themselves to the last, and of civil and martial men straining together in the fight.

sentences.zh: 凡厥勳勤，宜時銓序，可符列上。

translations.literal: Every service and toil should be weighed and ranked in due time—let the rolls be submitted.」
translations.idiomatic: Every deed and every strain should be weighed and ranked in season—let the lists come up.」

sentences.zh: 」盤龍愛妾杜氏，上送金鑷二十枚，手敕曰「餉周公阿杜」。

translations.literal: 」Panlong's beloved concubine Lady Du—the emperor sent her twenty gold hairpins, with a note in his own hand: 「A gift for Duke Zhou's darling Du.」
translations.idiomatic: 」To Panlong's beloved Lady Du the throne sent twenty gold hairpins, with a note in its own hand: 「For Duke Zhou's darling Du.」

sentences.zh: 轉太子左率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 改授持節，軍主如故。

translations.literal: He was re-commissioned with full credentials; his army command stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was given full credentials; his army command was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年，虜寇淮陽，圍角城。

translations.literal: The next year the northerners raided Huaiyang and besieged Jiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the northerners struck Huaiyang and laid siege to Jiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 先是上遣軍主成買戍角城，謂人曰：「我今作角城戍，我兒當得一子。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had sent army commander Cheng Mai to garrison Jiaocheng; he told people: 「I am now garrisoning Jiaocheng; my son ought to gain a grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the throne had sent army commander Cheng Mai to hold Jiaocheng. He told those around him: 「I am posted now to garrison Jiaocheng—my son ought to get himself a grandson.

sentences.zh: 」或問其故？

translations.literal: 」Someone asked why?
translations.idiomatic: 」Someone asked what he meant.

sentences.zh: 買曰「：角城與虜同岸，危險具多，我豈能使虜不敢南向。

translations.literal: Mai said: 「Jiaocheng stands on the same bank as the northerners; danger is on every side. How could I make them never dare look south?
translations.idiomatic: Mai said: 「Jiaocheng shares the riverbank with the northerners, and every sort of peril is at hand. I cannot make them never dare look south.

sentences.zh: 我若不沒虜，則應破虜。

translations.literal: If I do not perish among them, I should break them.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not die among them, I must break them.

sentences.zh: 兒不作孝子，便當作世子也。

translations.literal: If my son will not play the filial mourner, he will have to play the heir.」
translations.idiomatic: If my son will not stand as filial mourner, he will have to stand as heir.」

sentences.zh: 」至虜圍買數重，上遣領軍將軍李安民爲都督救之。

translations.literal: 」When the northerners had ringed Mai in several lines, the emperor sent Commander of the Palace Guards Li Anmin as overseer to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: 」When the northerners had closed ring after ring around Mai, the throne sent Commander of the Palace Guards Li Anmin as overseer to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 敕盤龍曰：「角城漣口，賊始復進，西道便是無賊，卿可率馬步下淮陰就李領軍。

translations.literal: He ordered Panlong: 「Jiaocheng and Lian Mouth—the enemy have only just resumed their advance; the western route is free of them. You can lead horse and foot down to Huaiyin to join Commander Li.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Panlong: 「Jiaocheng and Lian Mouth—the enemy have only just pushed forward again, and the western road is clear. Lead horse and foot down to Huaiyin and fall in with Commander Li.

sentences.zh: 鍾離船少，政可致衣仗數日糧，軍人扶淮步下也。

translations.literal: There are few boats at Zhongli; you need only enough food, gear, and rations for a few days—the men can march down along the Huai on foot.」
translations.idiomatic: Boats are scarce at Zhongli; carry only clothes, arms, and a few days' grain—the men can come down the Huai on foot.」

sentences.zh: 」買與虜拒戰，手所傷殺無數。

translations.literal: Mai fought the northerners; with his own hand he killed and wounded beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Mai met the northerners in battle and, with his own hand, killed and wounded beyond count.

sentences.zh: 晨朝早起，手中忽見有數升血，其日遂戰死。

translations.literal: Rising early in the morning, he suddenly found several pints of blood in his hand; that same day he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early and found several pints of blood suddenly in his palm; that same day he fell in the fight.

sentences.zh: 盤龍子奉叔單馬率二百餘人陷陣，虜萬餘騎張左右翼圍繞之，一騎走還，報奉叔已沒，盤龍方食，棄箸，馳馬奮槊，直奔虜陣，自稱「周公來！

translations.literal: Panlong's son Fengshu, alone on horseback, led a little over two hundred men into the enemy line; more than ten thousand northern horsemen spread left and right wings and surrounded them. One rider ran back reporting Fengshu was lost; Panlong was at his meal, cast down his chopsticks, spurred his horse with levelled lance, and charged straight into the northern ranks, crying 「Duke Zhou is here!
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's son Fengshu, alone on one horse, drove a little over two hundred men into the enemy line. More than ten thousand northern riders spread wings left and right and closed around them. One horseman galloped back saying Fengshu was down. Panlong was at table, dropped his chopsticks, spurred out with lance levelled, and charged straight into the northern ranks, shouting, 「Duke Zhou is here!

sentences.zh: 」虜素畏盤龍驍名，卽時披靡。

translations.literal: 」The northerners had long feared Panlong's fierce name; at once they broke.
translations.idiomatic: 」The northerners had long feared Panlong's name in battle; at once they scattered.

sentences.zh: 時奉叔已大殺虜，得出在外，盤龍不知，乃衝東擊西，奔南突北，賊衆莫敢當。

translations.literal: Fengshu had already slain great numbers of the enemy and gotten out; Panlong did not know it and still thrust east, struck west, ran south, burst north—the enemy masses dared not stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu had already cut down great numbers and fought his way clear, but Panlong did not know it. He still drove east, struck west, ran south, and burst north, and the enemy masses dared not meet him.

sentences.zh: 奉叔見其父久不出，復躍馬入陣。

translations.literal: Fengshu saw his father had not come out for a long while and leapt his horse back into the line.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu saw his father had not emerged for a long while and spurred back into the press.

sentences.zh: 父子兩匹騎，縈攪數萬人，虜衆大敗。

translations.literal: Father and son, two horses alone, wheeled and tangled among tens of thousands; the northern masses were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son on two horses alone wheeled and tore through tens of thousands; the northern host broke completely.

sentences.zh: 盤龍父子由是名播北國。

translations.literal: Panlong father and son thereby made their names known in the northern lands.
translations.idiomatic: By that fight Panlong and his son made their names thunder through the northern lands.

sentences.zh: 形甚羸訥，而臨軍勇果，諸將莫逮。

translations.literal: His bearing was very lean and slow of speech, yet facing battle he was brave and resolute—none of the generals could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He looked frail and spoke slowly, yet in battle he was fierce and sure—no general could keep pace with him.

sentences.zh: ，遷征虜將軍、南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: , he was moved to General Who Punishes the Barbarians and administrator of South Langye.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to General Who Punishes the Barbarians and administrator of South Langye.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷右衞將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to General of the Right Guard, with added appointment as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he became General of the Right Guard, with palace attendant added to his charge.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉大司馬，加征虜將軍、濟陽太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Grand Marshal, with added rank as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and administrator of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was moved to Grand Marshal, with General Who Punishes the Barbarians and administrator of Jiyang added.

sentences.zh: 世祖數講武，常令盤龍領馬軍，校騎騁槊。

translations.literal: Shizu often held military reviews and regularly had Panlong lead the horse army, matching riders in the lance charge.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu often held war drills and regularly set Panlong at the head of the horse army, pitting riders against one another in the charging lance.

sentences.zh: 後以疾爲光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later, because of illness, he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later, laid low by illness, he was named Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 尋出爲持節、都督兖州緣淮諸軍事、平北將軍、兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as bearer of credentials, overseer of Yanzhou and all military affairs along the Huai, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out bearing credentials as overseer of Yanzhou and of all armies along the Huai, as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 進爵爲侯。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 角城戍將張蒲，與虜潛相構結，因大霧乘船入清中採樵，載虜二十餘人，藏仗纖下，直向城東門，防門不禁，仍登岸拔白爭門。

translations.literal: Jiaocheng garrison commander Zhang Pu had secretly joined with the northerners; taking advantage of heavy fog, he boated into the Qing to gather firewood, loaded more than twenty northerners, hid weapons beneath thin matting, and drove straight for the east gate—the gate guards did not stop them—and came ashore, raised white banners, and fought for the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu, garrison commander at Jiaocheng, had secretly dealt with the northerners. In heavy fog he took a boat up the Qing on the pretext of gathering firewood, carried more than twenty of the enemy aboard with weapons hidden under thin matting, and made straight for the east gate. The guards let them through; they landed, raised white banners, and stormed the gate.

sentences.zh: 戍主皇甫仲賢率軍主孟靈寶等三十餘人於門拒戰，斬三人，賊衆被創赴水，而虜軍馬步至城外已三千餘人，阻塹不得進。

translations.literal: Garrison chief Huangfu Zhongxian led army commanders Meng Lingbao and more than thirty men to resist at the gate, cut down three, and many of the rebels, wounded, threw themselves into the water; but northern horse and foot at the wall already numbered more than three thousand and were blocked by the moat and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison chief Huangfu Zhongxian led Meng Lingbao and thirty-odd army commanders to hold the gate, killed three, and drove the wounded into the water; yet more than three thousand northern horse and foot were already at the wall, held back by the moat and unable to press in.

sentences.zh: 淮陰軍主王僧慶等領五百人赴救，虜衆乃退。

translations.literal: Huaiyin army commander Wang Sengqing and others led five hundred men to the rescue, and the northerners withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengqing of Huaiyin and others rushed five hundred men to the relief, and the northerners drew off.

sentences.zh: 坐爲有司所奏，詔白衣領職。

translations.literal: Because of this he was impeached by the relevant offices; an edict had him serve in plain robes while retaining his post.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices impeached him for it; an edict stripped his insignia yet left him in office, serving in plain robes.

sentences.zh: 八座尋奏復位。

translations.literal: The Eight Seats soon memorialized to restore his position.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Seats soon memorialized, and his rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 加領東平太守。

translations.literal: He was given the added charge of administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 盤龍表年老才弱，不可鎮邊，求解職，見許，還爲散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Panlong memorialized that he was old and his talents weak, unfit to guard the frontier, and asked to resign his post; permission was granted, and he returned as supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong wrote that age had thinned his strength and he was no longer fit to hold the border, and begged to be released; the throne agreed, and he came back as supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 世祖戲之曰：「卿著貂蟬，何如兜鍪？

translations.literal: The Shizu emperor joked with him: 「You wear the cicada clasp—how does that compare with a helmet?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu teased him: 「You wear the court cicada—how does that sit beside a helm?

sentences.zh: 」盤龍曰：「此貂蟬從兜鍪中出耳。

translations.literal: 」Panlong said: 「This cicada clasp came out of a helmet, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: 」Panlong answered, 「This cicada came out of a helmet in the first place.

sentences.zh: 」十一年，病卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: 」In the eleventh year he died of illness, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: 」In year eleven he died of illness, at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、兖州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was honored as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yanzhou.

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 子 奉叔

translations.literal: Son Fengshu
translations.idiomatic: Son Fengshu

translations.literal: [=] Section divider in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: [=] Section divider in the source text.

sentences.zh: 子奉叔，勇力絕人，隨盤龍征討，所在爲暴掠。

translations.literal: His son Fengshu had strength and courage beyond other men; he followed Panlong on campaigns and everywhere plundered violently.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengshu was a man of preternatural force; on every campaign with Panlong he led his men in brutal pillage.

sentences.zh: 世祖使領軍東討唐宇之，奉叔畏上威嚴，檢勒部下，不敢侵斥。

translations.literal: When the Shizu emperor sent the army east under its commander to attack Tang Yuzhi, Fengshu feared the throne's stern majesty, tightened discipline over his subordinates, and dared not plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu set the host east under its commander to crush Tang Yuzhi, Fengshu feared the emperor's wrath, reined in his men, and dared not lay hands on the countryside.

sentences.zh: 爲東宮直閤。

translations.literal: He was made a direct attendant of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was named a direct attendant of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 鬱林在西州，奉叔密得自進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Fei was in the Western Quarter, Fengshu won secret access to advance himself.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Fei still held the Western Quarter, Fengshu found a private way to court favor.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，與直閤將軍曹道剛爲心膂。

translations.literal: When Fei took the throne, he and Direct-Attendance General Cao Daogang became the emperor's right and left hands.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fei reigned, he and Direct-Attendance General Cao Daogang became the emperor's closest blades at his side.

sentences.zh: 道剛驍騎將軍，加冠軍將軍；

translations.literal: Daogang was made General of Valiant Cavalry, with the added rank of General Who Wins Every Battle;
translations.idiomatic: Daogang was raised to General of Valiant Cavalry, with General Who Wins Every Battle added to his title;

sentences.zh: 奉叔游擊將軍，加輔國將軍：竝監殿內直衞。

translations.literal: Fengshu was made General of Mobile Warfare, with the added rank of General Who Assists the State: both supervised the inner palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu was made General of Mobile Warfare, with General Who Assists the State added: together they commanded the inner palace guard.

sentences.zh: 少日，仍遷道剛爲黃門郎，高宗固諫不納。

translations.literal: Within a few days Daogang was moved to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; Emperor Ming remonstrated firmly but the emperor would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Daogang was shifted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; Emperor Ming protested in vain, and the appointment stood.

sentences.zh: 奉叔善騎馬，帝從其學騎射，尤見親寵，得入後宮。

translations.literal: Fengshu was skilled at riding; the emperor learned horsemanship and archery from him and favored him above others, so that he might enter the rear apartments.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu rode superbly; the emperor took horse and bow from him and showered him with favor so intimate that he was admitted to the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 尋加領淮陵太守、兖州中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made administrator of Huailing and impartial nominee for Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also named administrator of Huailing and impartial nominee for Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 道剛加南濮陽太守。

translations.literal: Daogang was made administrator of South Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daogang was made administrator of South Puyang.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，除黃門郎，未拜，仍出爲持節、都督青冀二州軍事、冠軍將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; before he could take up the seal he was sent out as bearer of credentials, overseer of Qing and Ji military affairs, General Who Wins Every Battle, and inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Longchang year 1 he was named Gentleman of the Yellow Gate; before the investiture reached him he went out bearing credentials to command Qing and Ji, as General Who Wins Every Battle and inspector of Qing.

sentences.zh: 時帝謀誅宰輔，故出奉叔爲外援，除道剛中軍司馬、青冀二州中正，本官如故。

translations.literal: The emperor was then plotting to kill his chief ministers, and so sent Fengshu out as outside support; Daogang was made army aide of the central corps and impartial nominee for Qing and Ji, his original posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was plotting the slaughter of his chief ministers and sent Fengshu out as outside muscle; Daogang was made army aide of the central corps and impartial nominee for Qing and Ji, while keeping his former titles.

sentences.zh: 奉叔就帝求千戶侯，許之。

translations.literal: Fengshu asked the emperor for a marquisate of a thousand households; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu begged the throne for a marquisate of a thousand households, and the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 高宗輔政，以爲不可，封曲江縣男，三百戶，奉叔大怒，於衆中攘刀厲目，高宗說喻之，乃受。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming held the regency he held this excessive; Fengshu was enfeoffed only as Baron of Qujiang, three hundred households. Fengshu flew into a rage, seized a blade in the assembly and glared; Emperor Ming reasoned with him until he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming's regency the grant was judged too lavish; Fengshu was given only Baron of Qujiang at three hundred households. He erupted in the hall, snatched a blade and glared; Ming talked him down until he took the seal.

sentences.zh: 奉叔辭畢將之鎮，部伍已出。

translations.literal: Fengshu finished his leave-taking and was about to go to his command; his troops had already marched out.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu had made his farewells and was setting out for his post; his columns were already beyond the gates.

sentences.zh: 高宗慮其一出不可復制，與蕭諶謀，稱敕召奉叔於省內殺之，勇士數人拳擊久之乃死。

translations.literal: Ming feared that once Fengshu left he could not be controlled again; with Xiao Chen he plotted, and under pretense of an edict summoned Fengshu within the ministry and killed him—several braves beat him with their fists for a long time before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Ming feared that once Fengshu reached his command he would never be reined in again. With Xiao Chen he forged a summons in the emperor's name, drew Fengshu into the ministry, and killed him—several strongmen pummeled him at length before he died.

sentences.zh: 啓帝云：「奉叔慢朝廷。

translations.literal: He reported to the emperor: 「Fengshu showed contempt for the court.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the emperor, 「Fengshu has shown contempt for the court.

sentences.zh: 」帝不獲已，可其奏。

translations.literal: 」The emperor, having no choice, approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor, with no room to refuse, approved the report.

sentences.zh: 高宗廢帝之日，道剛直閤省，蕭諶先入戶，若欲論事，兵人隨後奄進，以刀刺之，洞胷死，因進宮內廢帝。

translations.literal: On the day Ming deposed the emperor, Daogang was in the Direct-Attendance office; Xiao Chen entered the door first as though to discuss business, and soldiers following hard behind rushed in and stabbed him through the chest to death, then entered the palace to depose the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Ming deposed the emperor, Daogang was in the Direct-Attendance quarters. Xiao Chen went in ahead as if on ordinary business; soldiers hard on his heels burst through and ran Daogang through the chest, then entered the palace to unseat the emperor.

sentences.zh: 奉叔弟世雄，永元中，爲西江督護。

translations.literal: Fengshu's younger brother Shixiong, in the Yongyuan era, was protector of the West River.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshu's younger brother Shixiong, in the Yongyuan years, held the West River protectorship.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達事後，世雄殺廣州刺史蕭季敞，稱季敞同逆，送首京師。

translations.literal: After Chen Xianda's affair, Shixiong killed Inspector of Guangzhou Xiao Jichang, claiming Jichang had joined the rebellion, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Xianda's rising, Shixiong killed Xiao Jichang, inspector of Guangzhou, called him a fellow rebel, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史顏討殺之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Guangzhou Yan Tao killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tao, inspector of Guangzhou, put him to death.

sentences.zh: 王廣之

translations.literal: Wang Guangzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi

sentences.zh: 王廣之字林之，沛郡相人也。

translations.literal: Wang Guangzhi, styled Linzhi, was a man of Xiang in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi, styled Linzhi, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 少好弓馬，便捷有勇力。

translations.literal: In youth he loved bow and horse; he was quick and possessed of courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he lived for bow and saddle; he was light on his feet and fearless in strength.

sentences.zh: 初爲馬隊主。

translations.literal: He first served as chief of the horse company.
translations.idiomatic: He began as chief of a horse company.

sentences.zh: 宋大明中，以功補本縣令，殿中，龍驤，強弩將軍，驃騎中兵，南譙太守。

translations.literal: In the Daming era of Song, for merit he was made magistrate of his native county, palace attendant, dragon-charger, general of powerful crossbows, middle army officer of the Rapid Cavalry, and administrator of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song in the Daming era, for merit he became magistrate of his home county, then palace attendant, dragon-charger, general of powerful crossbows, middle army officer on the Rapid Cavalry staff, and administrator of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，除寧朔將軍、軍主，隷寧朔將軍劉懷珍征殷琰於壽春。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was made General Who Establishes the North and army commander, and followed General Who Establishes the North Liu Huaizhen in campaigning against Yin Yan at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi he was named General Who Establishes the North and army commander, and marched with Liu Huaizhen, General Who Establishes the North, against Yin Yan at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 琰將劉從築壘拒守，臺軍相守移日。

translations.literal: Yan's general Liu Cong built fortifications to hold them off; the imperial armies faced one another for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's general Liu Cong threw up ramparts and held; the imperial hosts stared at one another across the lines for day after day.

sentences.zh: 琰遣長史杜叔寶領五千人運車五百乘援從。
