translations.literal: Yan sent Chief Clerk Du Shubao at the head of five thousand men with five hundred supply carts to relieve Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Chief Clerk Du Shubao with five thousand men and five hundred supply carts to relieve Cong.

sentences.zh: 懷珍遣廣之及軍主辛慶祖、黃回、千道連等要擊於橫塘。

translations.literal: Huaizhen sent Guangzhi and army commanders Xin Qingzu, Huang Hui, Qian Daolian, and others to intercept them at Hengtang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen sent Guangzhi with army commanders Xin Qingzu, Huang Hui, Qian Daolian, and others to cut them at Hengtang.

sentences.zh: 寶結營拒戰，廣之等肉薄攻營，自晡至日沒，大敗之，殺傷千餘人，遂退，燒其運車。

translations.literal: Shubao formed a camp to resist; Guangzhi and the others pressed the attack at close quarters; from the hour before dusk until sunset they inflicted a great defeat, killing and wounding more than a thousand, then withdrew and burned the supply carts.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao made camp and stood to fight; Guangzhi and his fellows closed to hand-strokes. From late afternoon until the sun sank they broke the enemy, killing and wounding more than a thousand, then pulled back and put the supply train to the torch.

sentences.zh: 從聞之，棄壘奔走。

translations.literal: When Cong heard of it, he abandoned his ramparts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong heard, he threw down his works and ran.

sentences.zh: 時合肥城反，官軍前後受敵，都督劉勉召諸軍主會議。

translations.literal: At that time Hefei city had risen in revolt; the government host was caught between enemies fore and aft, and Area Commander Liu Mian summoned the army chiefs to council.
translations.idiomatic: Hefei had turned rebel; the imperial columns were boxed fore and aft, and Liu Mian, area commander, called the army chiefs into council.

sentences.zh: 廣之曰：「請得將軍所乘馬往平之。

translations.literal: Guangzhi said: 「Let me take the mount the general rides and go to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi said, 「Grant me the horse Your Lordship rides, and I will go settle this.

sentences.zh: 」勉以馬與廣之，廣之去三日，攻剋合肥賊。

translations.literal: 」Mian gave him the horse; Guangzhi was gone three days and stormed Hefei, overcoming the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: 」Mian gave him the mount; in three days Guangzhi had stormed Hefei and broken the rebels.

sentences.zh: 仍隨懷珍討淮北。

translations.literal: He then followed Huaizhen in the campaign on Huai north.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched with Huaizhen to pacify the Huai north.

sentences.zh: 時明帝遣青州刺史明僧暠北徵至三城，爲沈文秀所攻。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ming had sent Qingzhou Inspector Ming Sengchao on the northern expedition as far as Sancheng; he was attacked by Shen Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Ming had sent Ming Sengchao of Qingzhou north as far as Sancheng; Shen Wenxiu fell on him.

sentences.zh: 廣之將步騎三千餘人，緣海救之，俱引退。

translations.literal: Guangzhi led more than three thousand foot and horse along the coast to relieve him, and both sides drew off.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi took three thousand-odd foot and horse along the coast to relieve him; both hosts pulled back.

sentences.zh: 廣之又進軍襲文秀所置長廣太守劉桃根，桃根棄城走。

translations.literal: Guangzhi advanced again to strike Liu Taogen, whom Wenxiu had set over Changguang, and Taogen abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi pushed on again against Liu Taogen, Wenxiu's man in Changguang; Taogen fled the city.

sentences.zh: 軍還，封安蠻縣子，三百戶。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anman with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Anman, three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋改蒲圻。

translations.literal: Soon his fief was changed to Puqi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the fief was shifted to Puqi.

sentences.zh: 除建威將軍、南陽太守，不之官。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Nanyang, but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general who establishes might and administrator of Nanyang, yet never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 除越騎校尉，龍驤將軍、鍾離太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Volant Cavalry, Dragon-soaring General, and Administrator of Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commandant of volant cavalry, dragon-soaring general, and administrator of Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 遷爲左軍將軍，加寧朔將軍、高平太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Left Army, with added rank as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to general of the left army, with general who pacifies the north and administrator of Gaoping added.

sentences.zh: 又除游擊將軍，寧朔如故。

translations.literal: He was also made Mobile Strike General, with Pacifies North unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named mobile-strike general, keeping pacifies-the-north as before.

sentences.zh: 加給事中，冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was given attendant within the palace and the rank of Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: He was given attendant within the palace and raised to champion general.

sentences.zh: 討宋建平，先登京口，改封寧都縣子，五百戶。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Jianping under Song, he was first over the Jingkou wall; his fief was changed to Viscount of Ningdu with five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Song's Jianping he was first up the Jingkou rampart; his fief was changed to Viscount of Ningdu, five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太祖廢蒼梧，出廣之爲假節、督徐州軍事、徐州刺史、鍾離太守，冠軍如故。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor deposed Cangwu, he sent Guangzhi out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of Xuzhou Military Affairs, Inspector of Xuzhou, and Administrator of Zhongli, with Champion unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor cast down Cangwu, he sent Guangzhi out with the staff as commander of Xuzhou military affairs, inspector of Xuzhou, and administrator of Zhongli, champion as before.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，廣之留京師，豫平石頭，仍從太祖頓新亭，進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, Guangzhi stayed in the capital, took part in pacifying Stone City, then followed the Grand Ancestor to camp at Xinting and was advanced to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, Guangzhi remained in the capital, helped pacify Stone City, then followed the Grand Ancestor to Xinting and was raised to general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 太祖誅黃回。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor executed Huang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor put Huang Hui to death.

sentences.zh: 回弟駟及從弟馬、兄子奴亡逸。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Si, his cousin Ma, and his brother's son Nu fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Si, his cousin Ma, and his brother's son Nu broke loose and vanished.

sentences.zh: 太祖與廣之書曰：「黃回雖有微勳，而罪過轉不可容。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor wrote Guangzhi: 「Huang Hui had slight merit, but his crimes grew past bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor wrote Guangzhi: 「Huang Hui did some small service, yet his offenses piled until they could no longer be borne.

sentences.zh: 近遂啓請御大小二輿爲刺史服飾。

translations.literal: Lately he even petitioned for the imperial great and small carriages as an inspector's regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Only lately he asked for the throne's great and small carriages to dress an inspector's state.

sentences.zh: 吾乃不惜爲其啓聞，政恐得輿，復求畫輪車。

translations.literal: I was not unwilling to petition for him—only feared that once he had the carriages he would ask for painted-wheel chariots as well.
translations.idiomatic: I would not have refused to plead for him—only I dreaded that once the carriages were granted he would demand painted-wheel chariots next.

sentences.zh: 此外罪不可勝數，弟自悉之。

translations.literal: Besides, crimes too many to count—you know them yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, offenses beyond numbering—you know them as well as I.

sentences.zh: 今啓依法。

translations.literal: Now I petition according to law.」
translations.idiomatic: Now I move against him by law.」

sentences.zh: 」令廣之於江西搜捕駟等。

translations.literal: He ordered Guangzhi to search west of the river for Si and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Guangzhi to hunt west of the river for Si and his kin.

sentences.zh: ，進爵爲侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: , and advanced him to marquis with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to marquis with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍、左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and general of the left army.

sentences.zh: 北虜動，明年，詔假廣之節，出淮上。

translations.literal: The northern enemy stirred; the next year an edict gave Guangzhi the staff and sent him out on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners stirred; the next year an edict armed Guangzhi with the staff and sent him to the Huai line.

sentences.zh: 廣之家在彭、沛，啓上求招誘郷里部曲，北取彭城，上許之。

translations.literal: Guangzhi's family lay in Peng and Pei; he memorialized asking leave to recruit his native following and march north to take Pengcheng, and the throne granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi's kin were in Peng and Pei; he asked leave to raise his home bands and drive north on Pengcheng, and the throne assented.

sentences.zh: 以廣之爲使持節、都督淮北軍事、平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Guangzhi was made Bearer with Constant Staff, Commander of Huai-north Military Affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer with constant staff, commander of Huai-north military affairs, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣之引軍過淮，無所剋獲，坐免官。

translations.literal: Guangzhi led his host across the Huai but won nothing; for the failure he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi crossed the Huai with his column and took nothing; for that failure he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋除征虜將軍，加散騎常侍、太子右率。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians, with added rank as Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary and Right Leader of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named general who conquers the barbarians, with supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and right leader of the crown prince added.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，遷長沙王鎮軍司馬，南東海太守，司徒司馬，尋陽相，南新蔡太守，安陸王北中郎左軍司馬、廣陵太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Guangzhi was moved to army chief of staff to the Prince of Changsha, Administrator of South Donghai, Director of the Masters of Writing and army chief of staff, Xunyang grand administrator, Administrator of South Xincai, left-army chief of staff to the Prince of Anlu's Northern Center Colonel, and Administrator of Guangling, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu ascended, Guangzhi became army chief of staff to the Prince of Changsha, administrator of South Donghai, director of the masters of writing and army chief of staff, Xunyang grand administrator, administrator of South Xincai, left-army chief of staff to the Prince of Anlu's northern center colonel, and administrator of Guangling, still holding his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、都督徐州諸軍事、徐州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Bearer with Constant Staff, Commander of all Xuzhou Military Affairs, and Inspector of Xuzhou, his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out with constant staff as commander of all Xuzhou military affairs and inspector of Xuzhou, general's rank as before.

sentences.zh: 還爲光祿大夫、左將軍、司徒司馬。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Minister of the Imperial Clan, Left General, and Director of the Masters of Writing and army chief of staff.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made minister of the imperial clan, left general, and director of the masters of writing with army chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 遷右衞將軍，轉散騎常侍，前將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard, then to Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary and Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to general of the right guard, then to supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary and forward general.

sentences.zh: 世祖見廣之子珍國應堪大用，謂廣之曰：「卿可謂老蚌也。

translations.literal: Shizu saw that Guangzhi's son Zhenguo looked fit for great trust and told Guangzhi: 「You may be called an old oyster.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu saw Guangzhi's son Zhenguo and judged him fit for heavy charge; he told Guangzhi, 「You are the old oyster at last.

sentences.zh: 」廣之曰：「臣不敢辭。

translations.literal: Guangzhi said: 「Your servant dare not decline.」
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi said, 「Your servant dares not refuse the praise.」

sentences.zh: 」上大笑。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The throne laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 除游擊將軍，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Mobile Strike General but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was named mobile-strike general and would not take the seal.

sentences.zh: 十一年，虜動，假廣之節，招募。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the barbarians stirred; Guangzhi was given the staff to recruit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the enemy stirred; Guangzhi was armed with the staff to raise troops.

sentences.zh: ，遷給事中、左衞將軍。

translations.literal: , and was transferred to Attendant within the Palace and General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was then moved to attendant within the palace and general of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史崔慧景密與虜通，有異志。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of Yu Cui Huijing was in secret traffic with the barbarians and nursed a separate intent.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yu Cui Huijing was then in secret league with the enemy and harbored a private design.

sentences.zh: ，以廣之爲持節、督豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事、平西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: , and Guangzhi was made Bearer with Constant Staff, Commander of Military Affairs for Xiyang in Yuzhou and Runan in Sizhou west of that, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi was made bearer with constant staff, commander of military affairs for Xiyang in Yu and Runan in Si west of that, general who pacifies the west, and inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 預廢鬱林勳，增封三百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit in deposing Yulin, his fief was increased by three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For helping cast down Yulin, his fief gained three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高宗誅害諸王，遣廣之征安陸王子敬於江陽，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Gaozong killed the princes and sent Guangzhi to campaign against Prince Zijing of Anlu at Jiangyang, granting him one suite of martial pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong struck down the princes and sent Guangzhi against Prince Zijing of Anlu at Jiangyang, with one set of martial pipes.

sentences.zh: 事平，仍改授使持節、散騎常侍、都督江州諸軍事、鎮南將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was reassigned Bearer with Constant Staff, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of all Jiangzhou Military Affairs, General Who Guards the South, and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once it was done, he was reassigned constant staff, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, commander of all Jiangzhou military affairs, general who guards the south, and inspector of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 進封應城縣公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Yingcheng with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Yingcheng, fief two thousand households.

sentences.zh: ，虜圍司州，遣廣之持節督司州征討，解圍。

translations.literal: , and when the barbarians besieged Sizhou, Guangzhi was sent with the staff to command the Sizhou campaign and lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy ringed Sizhou, Guangzhi was sent with the staff to command the relief and break the siege.

sentences.zh: 廣之未至百餘里，虜退，乃還。

translations.literal: Guangzhi had not yet reached a hundred-odd li when the northerners withdrew, and he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi was still a hundred-odd li short when the northerners pulled back; he turned home.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷侍中、鎮軍將軍，給扶。

translations.literal: The next year he was moved to Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army, with a walking staff granted.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he became palace attendant and General Who Guards the Army, with staff support granted.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he died.

sentences.zh: 年七十三。

translations.literal: He was seventy-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、車騎將軍，諡曰莊公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Chariots and Cavalry; posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was Outer Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Chariots and Cavalry; posthumous name Duke Zhuang.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：公侯扞城，守國之所資也。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Dukes and marquises buttress the walls—what guarding the state relies upon.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: dukes and marquises hold the ramparts—the stuff on which guarding the realm rests.

sentences.zh: 必須久習兵事，非一戰之力。

translations.literal: One must long practice military affairs; it is not the strength of a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: They must season long in war; one fight will not do.

sentences.zh: 安國等致效累朝，聲勤克舉，竝識時變，咸知附託。

translations.literal: Anguo and the others rendered service through successive reigns, their repute and diligence achieved; all alike knew the changing times and understood where to attach trust.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo and his peers served reign after reign, their fame and toil fully paid; each read the turn of the age and knew where to pledge.

sentences.zh: 盤龍驍勇，獨冠三軍，匈奴之憚飛將，曾不若也。

translations.literal: Panlong was fierce and brave, alone topped the three armies—the Xiongnu dread of the Flying General did not come close.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong's fighting nerve stood alone atop the three armies; even the Xiongnu fear of the Flying General fell short.

sentences.zh: 壯矣哉！

translations.literal: How magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: How grand!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：安國舊將，協同遷社，同裨九江，翊從中夏。

translations.literal: In praise: Anguo, an old commander, joined in shifting the altars, aided together at Jiujiang, supported the central realm.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Anguo, veteran of the ranks, shared in shifting the state altars, bolstered Jiujiang as one, and steadied the central lands.

sentences.zh: 盤龍殺敵，洞開胡馬。

translations.literal: Panlong slew the foe and pierced open the Hu horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Panlong cut down enemies and broke the Hu horse-lines wide.

sentences.zh: 廣之末年，旌旄驟把。

translations.literal: Guangzhi in his later years suddenly seized banner and command staff.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi in his last years seized banner and staff at a stroke.
